text:
jamal_csm: Quick heads-up — Willow Health onboarding perf snapshot: p50 110ms, p95 360ms, p99 740ms. avg tokens/request ~ 420. Logged a steady cost uptick this week as traffic ramps. Thinking a small-model swap + int8 trial + weighted routing fallback to reduce unit cost without impacting latency SLA. PTAL.

maria_cs: Thanks Jamal. Do we have any signal on customer-side quality sensitivity? any ticket threads mentioning hallucinations or regressions?

jamal_csm: No active complaints yet. They do have a closed-loop QA set (about 200 prompts) from onboarding tests we can run. I can kick off an eval if eng/ML agrees on model candidates.

devon_se: I can run a quick canary. Proposed plan: 5% traffic -> redwood-small-v1-int8, 20% fallback to redwood-small-v1-fp16, rest stays on redwood-medium-v1. Monitor latency, token cost, and quality delta on the QA set. If QA regression <= 1.5% we ramp. Thoughts? :thinking_face:

priya_se: Sounds reasonable. Add an automated rollback trigger if QA failure > 2% or customer complaints > 5 in an hour. Also recommend validating top-5 intents for correctness (they're sensitive to short completions).

ethan_ml: Agree with canary numbers. Quick note: int8 tends to drop probability mass in long-tail rare token generation — could affect named-entity outputs. Suggest adding targeted evals for entity recall.

devon_se: Ops/config snippet I plan to push for the routing policy:

```yaml
route_policy:
  - name: willow-mini-canary
    weight: 0.05
    model: redwood-small-v1-int8
    fallback:
      - model: redwood-small-v1-fp16
        weight: 0.2
      - model: redwood-medium-v1
        weight: 0.75
    triggers:
      rollback_on:
        qa_delta_pct: 2.0
        customer_complaints_per_hour: 5
    metrics:
      - latency_p95
      - cost_per_1000_tokens
      - qa_delta
```

maria_cs: Can you also enable prefix/KV caching for their common prompts? I noticed a lot of repeated system + few-shot context. That could shave 30-40ms on warm flows.

devon_se: Good call. I'll enable prefix caching + 3s soft TTL for session tokens. Also enabling token-budget caps for high-latency tails (max_gen_tokens: 256) to cap cost spikes.

jamal_csm: I'll message the customer that we'll run a low-risk canary this week and share the QA snapshot results. Also collecting their ops contact to watch for perception.

ops_bot: Canary deployment scheduled: 1748530200. Canary ID: canary-willow-1748529630. Auto-monitoring enabled for latency, errors, and QA hook.

priya_se: One more request — capture sample outputs from both int8 and fp16 for the 20 highest-diff prompts so we can review qualitative differences before a full ramp.

ethan_ml: I'll prepare the diff runner and the eval notebook. ETA end of day tomorrow.

devon_se: Plan of record: start 5% int8 canary (routes + cache), collect QA and targeted entity recall, gather qualitative diffs, auto-rollback thresholds set. If QA delta <=1.5% and no complaint pattern after 6 hours, increase to 25% then to 60% over 48h.

maria_cs: Great. Jamal — can you confirm customer OK for the 5% test? I'll attach the customer comms template.

jamal_csm: Will do — sending now. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

maria_cs: Leaving action items here:
- jamal_csm: confirm customer approval + share ops contact (due EOD)
- devon_se: kick canary + enable prefix caching + token cap (start time 1748530200)
- ethan_ml: run diff eval + notebook (EOD tomorrow)
- priya_se: define QA rollback thresholds and entity recall tests (today)

jamal_csm: noted, will update thread when customer ack arrives.
